Definition
Definition
In this lesson, you will observe the operation of a typical FDM transmitter and receiver circuit.
INTRODUCTIONM
In the first part of the experiment, you will setup, align and observe the signals in the transmitter or multiplexer.
In the second part of the experiment, you will setup, align and observe the signals in the receiver or demultiplexer.
The circuits use four information sources and FM modulation.
The components used in these circuits are just FM modulators and demodulators.
By combining the FM modulators and demodulators, a FDM system is created.
It is important to note however, there are other ways to construct a FDM system, this is only one example.
This example will give you the basics of operating or maintaining any FDM system.

In this experiment, you will observe the operation and measure signals in a typical FDM receiver circuit.
EXPERIMENT
The receiver circuit is contained on PC130-325 and consists of the components necessary to support the five PLL FM demodulators.
The FDM signal is applied to pin 6 of the MAIN FM demodulator, IC1, through R1, a level control.
The center frequency is set by C3 and the loop gain is controlled by R4.
Note that the TTL output of the VCO is connected to the phase comparator, pins 9 to 3.
MEASUREMENT SETUP - Input to the Phase Comparator (IC1 pins 3 to 9) are from the VCO.
Even though digital signals are not used, the FDM signal input is not really a sine wave. Remember, the square wave output was used in the multiplexer.
The output of the MAIN demodulator is taken from pin 14, analog out, and applied to a buffer amplifier.
MEASUREMENT SETUP - The signal is outputted on IC1 pin 14 as the demodulated analog signal.
The buffer amplifier is used to boost the signal for suppling four different subcarrier demodulators.
Each of the four subcarrier demodulators are identical. Let's discuss CH1, or IC3 only.
The demodulated MAIN carrier is applied to pins 2 and 3, through a RC network, to the subcarrier demodulator.
Pins 4 and 5 are connected making the PLL circuit a FM demodulator.
R18 is used to set the center frequency.
The output from pin 7 is then amplified and filtered.
Each of the four outputs are on the CH1 to CH4 test points.
Now, pick up the PC130-325 card and compare to the schematic.
R1, R4 and C3 are the adjustments for the MAIN carrier demodulator.
R18, R23, R26 and R31 adjust the subcarrier demodulators.
